name: Baghmati
origin: Nepal Himalaya, near the Kathmandu Valley
note: Flows through the Bihar plains (past the West Champaran area) on its way toward the Kosi system and the Ganga.

name: Banas
note: Rises in Rajasthan and joins the Chambal — not to be confused with the separate Banas river in Gujarat, which drains into the Rann of Kutch.

name: Barakar
note: Main tributary of the Damodar.

name: Betwa
note: Joins the Yamuna near Hamirpur.

name: Burhi Gandak
note: Not to be confused with the Gandak (Gandaki) river — a separate tributary flowing entirely within Bihar, joining the Ganga in the Munger/Patna region.

name: Chambal
origin: Janapav Hills, Malwa Plateau, near Mhow/Indore, Madhya Pradesh (in the Vindhyan range)
note: The Gandhisagar Dam is built on the Chambal near Kota, Rajasthan. It flows through Bundi, Sawai Madhopur and Dholpur, and is famous for its badland topography — the Chambal Ravines. Joins the Yamuna near Etawah.

name: Damodar
note: Nicknamed the 'Sorrow of Bengal' for its historic floods. The Barakar is its main tributary. Joins the Hooghly rather than the Ganga's main channel.

name: Gandak
origin: Nepal Himalaya — formed by the Kaligandaki and Trishuli (the Gandaki system)
note: Distinct from the Burhi Gandak, a separate, smaller Bihar tributary of the Ganga. Joins the Ganga near Sonpur/Patna.

name: Ganga
origin: Gangotri Glacier, Uttarakhand (as the Bhagirathi; becomes the Ganga at Devprayag after joining the Alaknanda)
note: Flows through Kannauj, Prayagraj (confluence with the Yamuna), Chhapra, Patna, Sonpur and Munger. At Farakka Barrage it splits into the Padma (into Bangladesh) and the Hooghly (its distributary through West Bengal, via Diamond Harbour and Haldia Port).

name: Ghaghara
origin: Formed by the Kali (Uttarakhand) / Karnali (Nepal), sourced near the Mapcha Chungo Glacier, Tibet
note: Called the Karnali in Nepal. Its tributary the Sarda (Saryu) rises at the Milam Glacier (Goriganga) and runs along the India-Nepal border, where it is locally called the Kali or Chauk. The Ghaghara joins the Ganga near Chhapra.

name: Gomti
note: Flows past Lucknow before joining the Ganga near Ghazipur. The Sai river runs roughly parallel before merging in. (Source data only covers a partial stretch, so the drawn course is incomplete.)

name: Hooghly
note: The Ganga's principal distributary through West Bengal after Farakka Barrage, flowing past Diamond Harbour and Haldia Port to the Bay of Bengal. (Source data only covers a short digitised stretch, so the drawn course is partial.)

name: Johilla
note: A minor headwater tributary of the Son, near Amarkantak.

name: Kali Sindh
note: Joins the Chambal.

name: Ken
note: Joins the Yamuna near Banda. Subject of the Ken-Betwa river-linking project.

name: Kosi
origin: Formed by the Sun Kosi, Arun and Tamor rivers (Nepal Himalaya), which converge to form the Sapt Kosi
note: An antecedent river — it cuts across the rising Himalaya rather than being deflected by it. Historically called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' for its shifting course and floods.

name: Mahananda
note: Joins the Ganga near the Bihar-West Bengal border, close to where that border also meets Bangladesh.

name: North Koel
note: A tributary of the Son, rising in the Chota Nagpur Plateau, Jharkhand.

name: Parbati
note: A tributary of the Chambal in Madhya Pradesh.

name: Ramganga
note: Passes through Jim Corbett National Park; joins the Ganga near Kannauj. The Pilibhit and Dudhwa areas lie along its middle course in Uttar Pradesh.

name: Rapti
note: Flows past Gorakhpur before joining the Ghaghara.

name: Rihand
note: A tributary of the Son near the Ramgarh Hills. The Gobind Vallabh Pant Sagar reservoir — one of India's largest — is formed on the Rihand.

name: Sarda
note: Also called the Saryu; along the India-Nepal border it is known as the Kali or Chauk, and in Nepal this same river is called the Karnali. (Source data only covers a short stretch near the border, so the drawn course is partial.)

name: Sindh
note: Joins the Yamuna between the Chambal and Betwa confluences.

name: Son
origin: Amarkantak, Chhattisgarh (the same plateau as the Narmada's source)
note: The largest south-bank tributary of the Ganga. Its course runs Chhattisgarh → Madhya Pradesh → Uttar Pradesh → Bihar, joining the Ganga near Patna.

name: Tons
note: A left-bank Himalayan tributary joining the Yamuna near its source, before the river reaches Etawah.

name: Yamuna
note: Westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga. Runs through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh — past Etawah, Hamirpur and Banda — before joining the Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad). Left-bank tributaries (Tons, Hindan, Rind, Sengar, Varuna) are Himalayan/minor; right-bank tributaries (Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, Ken) drain the Vindhyan/peninsular side.
